risk_signals.statement: ROE more than tripled from a series-low 5.07% (FY2017) to 20.85% (FY2025), with NPL ratio falling from a series-high 7.67% (FY2015) to a series-low 2.73% (FY2025) over the same broad period. Unlike most other banks in this dataset, where recent years show emerging stress, Prime Bank shows a sustained, multi-year improvement in both profitability and asset quality simultaneously.

CAR jumped from 14.01% (FY2017) to 17.04% (FY2018) and has stayed in a strong 16.78%-18.07% range every year since — one of the highest and most consistent capital cushions of any bank researched in this dataset, comfortably above the regulatory minimum throughout the full 12-year series.

FY2016-2017 were the weakest years in the ANNUAL series (ROE 5.30% and 5.07% respectively, NPL 5.96% and 5.45%), a low point the bank has steadily moved away from in every year since. (Note: this characterization only holds within the FY2014-2025 annual/Q4 series -- see the newly-recovered 2013 quarterly result below, which is materially worse and predates this series entirely.)

A 2026-08-26 Q1-Q3 quarterly backfill recovered Prime Bank's true series low point, which predates its own annual/Q4 series entirely (that series only starts FY2014): Q1 2013 (Consolidated basis -- no separate Solo statement existed in that specific quarter's disclosure format) was a net LOSS of -1,517.36m (EPS -1.62). H1 2013 (Solo basis) was also a net loss, -679.33m (EPS -0.66) -- narrower than Q1 alone because Q2 2013 alone was profitable (~+838m, a figure that reconciles to within BDT 1 across three independently-sourced documents' comparative columns: the 2013 H1 filing itself, the 2014 Q1 filing's Jan-Mar'13 comparative, and the 2014 H1 filing's Apr-Jun'13 discrete comparative). Both losses were driven by a specific loan-loss provision spike (3,418m within H1 2013's 4,145m total provision, versus 436.7m in the prior-year H1). This is a materially worse single-period result than anything visible in the FY2014-2025 annual series, whose own 'weakest years' characterization (FY2016-2017, above) has zero visibility into 2011-2013.

insights.historical_context: Prime Bank presents one of the strongest and most consistent long-run improvement stories in this dataset: from a mid-2010s low point (FY2016-2017, ROE ~5%, NPL ~6%) to FY2025's series-best ROE (20.85%) and NPL ratio (2.73%), backed by a capital cushion that has remained comfortably above 16.7% for eight consecutive years. This trajectory is the inverse of the deterioration patterns seen at several other banks in this dataset (AB Bank, ICB Islamic Bank, Al-Arafah Islami Bank) and stands out even among the healthier banks (Trust Bank, Jamuna Bank, EBL) for the size and consistency of the multi-year gain.

sources.note: Found primebank.com.bd's own quarterly/half-yearly disclosure archive at https://www.primebank.com.bd/quarterly-half-yearly-reports (confirmed working, not WAF-blocked): 48 filings spanning 2010-2025 (Q1/Half-Yearly/Q3 every year) plus 2 more for 2026 (Q1, H1), matching the ~50-PDF estimate exactly. These periods' PDFs were genuine text-layer (non-scanned) and extracted cleanly with pdftotext -layout. Each document contains a Consolidated section followed by a Solo (Bank-only) section for both Balance Sheet and Profit & Loss; SOLO is used throughout per project convention. Q3 filings from 2016-2020 and ALL H1 filings show a 4-column P&L (cumulative + discrete-quarter, each with a comparative); the cumulative pair (first two columns) was used -- an initial parser pass mistakenly extracted the discrete-quarter columns for these, caught by re-deriving the Q2/Q3-2024 figures and cross-checking against the annual report's own embedded 'Quarterly Performance' table (see 2024 sources), then fixed and re-validated against every period. nav_per_share genuinely not disclosed in 2012, 2014, 2016, 2017, and the 2018 Q1 filing specifically (present from 2018 H1 onward) -- left null rather than fabricated. 2022 H1's 'borrowings' balance-sheet row lost its label text during extraction (note ref '12a' and the two amounts survived); position plus an exact liabilities-sum reconciliation (borrowings+deposits+other_liabilities=total_liabilities) confirms the value with high confidence.

These filings' PDFs were image-based (scanned), not text-layer -- 2010-2013 used a dense single-'poster'-page format (2011 H1 was an unusual 25MB/20400px-tall single page, sliced into vertical segments to read), 2015 Q1/Q3 and 2014 Q1/Q3 used an 8-page scanned format, 2025 Q3 was unexpectedly a 7.6MB scanned PDF despite every neighboring quarter being a normal ~0.8MB text PDF. Figures were read directly off high-resolution (150-300 DPI) page renders of the original documents -- NOT trusted from raw OCR text, which was demonstrably unreliable on a first pass (e.g. digit transpositions found and corrected in 2012 Q1 and 2013 Q3 total_liabilities via the balance-sheet identity check; several 2011 Q3/2012 Q3/2013 Q3 P&L figures were mis-transcribed on an initial read and had to be re-verified against a zoomed crop). Every period's balance-sheet identity (assets=liabilities+equity) and P&L arithmetic chain (opincome-opexpense=opprofit; opprofit-provision=PBT; PBT-tax=PAT) reconciles exactly. A best-effort Tesseract OCR transcript of the same pages is kept in annual_reports/PRIMEBANK/ as *-ocr.txt for reference/future re-verification, but is not itself the source of the JSON figures. 2010 Q1 and Q3 are CONSOLIDATED-ONLY (this vintage's Q1/Q3 disclosure format had no separate Solo section at all, unlike its own H1 filing which did); 2013 Q1 is also CONSOLIDATED-ONLY (used an older thin single-page template unlike the taller dual-section format its own Q3 filing used that same year) -- both explicitly flagged per project convention.
